faqs.q: What is 10DLC and is it mandatory for sending wholesale SMS to the USA?
faqs.a: Yes. 10DLC (10-Digit Long Code) is the cellular standard regulated by the CTIA and mobile operators (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile). Any application sending A2P messages over local US long codes must be registered with The Campaign Registry (TCR). NAMX Telecom handles brand and campaign vetting to assign legitimate campaign IDs and avoid carrier blocking.

faqs.q: Can I use alphanumeric Sender IDs (like 'MYCOMPANY') in the USA?
faqs.a: No. Mobile networks in the United States and Canada do not support alphanumeric sender headers. All SMS messages must originate from a verified 10DLC number, a Toll-Free number (8XX), or a 5-6 digit Short Code.

faqs.q: What are the carrier pass-through surcharges for US SMS traffic?
faqs.a: US carriers charge pass-through fees (typically $0.002 to $0.004 per SMS segment) depending on whether the campaign is registered under 10DLC. NAMX Telecom offers all-inclusive billing rate cards or separated wholesale rate models for transparent accounting.

faqs.q: How long does 10DLC registration take?
faqs.a: Brand registration is usually quick once company details match official records. Campaign vetting by the carriers commonly takes from a few days to a couple of weeks, depending on the use case and how complete the sample messages and opt-in description are.

faqs.q: Can I send SMS to Canada on the same route as the USA?
faqs.a: No. Canada shares the +1 country code but has separate carriers (Bell, Rogers, Telus and regional operators) and different rules. 10DLC registration is a US scheme, so Canadian traffic is routed and priced separately.

faqs.q: Why are some US messages delivered without a DLR?
faqs.a: Some US routes return intermediate or carrier-level receipts rather than handset receipts. Check the DLR status and error code fields; a missing final receipt does not always mean the message failed, but persistent gaps should be raised with the NOC.

guideIntro: The United States is one of the most regulated A2P SMS markets in the world. Unlike most countries, US mobile networks do not accept alphanumeric sender IDs, so every business message must come from a registered 10-digit long code (10DLC), a verified toll-free number, or a leased short code. Unregistered traffic is filtered or blocked by the carriers, so registration comes before pricing when you plan US delivery.

Throughput in the US depends on registration quality, not only on your provider. For 10DLC, The Campaign Registry (TCR) assigns each brand a trust score after vetting, and the carriers use that score and the campaign use case to set message limits — AT&T per-minute throughput and T-Mobile daily caps, for example. A well-documented brand and campaign usually gets far more capacity than a thin registration.
checklist: Register your brand (legal company name, EIN, website, contact) with The Campaign Registry.
Register each campaign with its use case (2FA, account notifications, marketing, etc.) and sample messages.
Collect and store opt-in consent; for marketing, consent must be explicit and documented under the TCPA.
Support STOP and HELP keywords and honour opt-outs immediately.
Keep restricted content (often summarised as SHAFT: sex, hate, alcohol, firearms, tobacco) out of standard campaigns.
For toll-free numbers, complete toll-free verification before sending — unverified toll-free traffic is blocked.

faqs.q: Are dynamic alphanumeric sender IDs allowed in the UK?
faqs.a: Yes. The UK fully supports dynamic alphanumeric sender IDs up to 11 characters (e.g. 'YOURBRAND'). However, sender IDs must not be misleading or impersonate financial institutions without prior authorization.

faqs.q: How does NAMX handle UK Mobile Number Portability (MNP)?
faqs.a: Our routing platform executes real-time HLR queries against the UK centralized porting database before message dispatch, ensuring zero routing delays when a subscriber has moved between EE, Vodafone, O2, or Three.

faqs.q: Do OTP and delivery notification SMS need consent in the UK?
faqs.a: Service messages that the customer needs, such as OTP codes, order and delivery updates, are not marketing under PECR and do not need marketing consent. Mixing promotional content into these messages turns them into marketing, so keep them separate.

faqs.q: Which mobile networks operate in the UK?
faqs.a: The main networks are EE (BT Group), Virgin Media O2, and VodafoneThree, formed when Vodafone UK and Three UK merged in 2025. Many MVNOs such as Tesco Mobile, Giffgaff and Sky Mobile run on these networks, so HLR/MNP lookup is used to route ported numbers correctly.

guideIntro: The United Kingdom is an open, mature SMS market: alphanumeric sender IDs of up to 11 characters are widely supported and there is no pre-registration scheme like India's DLT. That makes it easy to start sending, but it also makes the UK a target for sender ID spoofing, so brand-protection measures and consent rules matter more than technical registration.

Marketing SMS in the UK is governed by the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations (PECR), enforced by the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), together with UK GDPR. Transactional messages such as OTPs and delivery updates do not need marketing consent, but promotional messages do — with a narrow 'soft opt-in' for existing customers buying similar products. The Mobile Ecosystem Forum (MEF) runs the SMS SenderID Protection Registry, which lets banks and other brands block unauthorised use of their sender names.
checklist: Use a sender ID that clearly identifies your brand; misleading sender IDs breach PECR and operator rules.
Get prior consent for marketing SMS (or rely on the soft opt-in for existing customers) and record it.
Include a simple, free opt-out in every marketing message, e.g. 'Reply STOP'.
If your brand is often impersonated, register your sender ID with the MEF SenderID Protection Registry.
Use numeric long codes when you need two-way replies — alphanumeric senders cannot receive replies.

faqs.q: How long does TDRA Sender ID registration take in the UAE?
faqs.a: Standard TDRA registration takes 3 to 5 business days. Our regulatory desk assists enterprise clients with Trade License and authorization letter paperwork to expedite approval.

faqs.q: Does NAMX support Arabic language SMS concatenation in the UAE?
faqs.a: Yes. We support 16-bit UCS-2 Unicode encoding with UDH concatenation for multi-part Arabic messages up to 1,000 characters without corruption.

faqs.q: Can I send promotional SMS in the UAE at night?
faqs.a: No. Promotional messages are restricted to 7:00–21:00 UAE time (GST, UTC+4). Messages submitted outside the window should be queued and released when it opens; transactional and OTP messages are not restricted.

faqs.q: How many characters can an Arabic SMS contain?
faqs.a: Arabic requires UCS-2 encoding, so a single SMS holds 70 characters. Longer messages are split into segments of 67 characters each, and each segment is billed separately.

guideIntro: The UAE is a pre-registration market: every sender ID used for business SMS must be registered and approved before traffic is accepted by e& (Etisalat) and du. Messages from unregistered sender IDs are typically blocked or delivered with a generic header, so sender ID registration is the first step of any UAE launch.

The Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA) sets the rules. Promotional SMS can only be delivered between 7:00 and 21:00 UAE time, must carry an opt-out, and promotional sender IDs are identified with an 'AD-' prefix. Transactional and OTP traffic can be sent 24/7. Because many recipients read Arabic, plan for UCS-2 encoding, which cuts a single SMS to 70 characters.
checklist: Register each sender ID with the operators before sending, supplying your trade licence and an authorisation letter.
Separate promotional and transactional sender IDs — promotional senders carry the 'AD-' prefix.
Schedule promotional campaigns inside the 7:00–21:00 local window.
Include an opt-out instruction in every promotional message.
Use UCS-2 for Arabic content and budget for the 70 / 67 character segment limits.

faqs.q: What DLT parameters must be submitted via SMPP in India?
faqs.a: When binding via SMPP to NAMX Telecom for Indian termination, each submit_sm PDU must include TLV parameters for Principal Entity ID (PE_ID) and Content Template ID (Template_ID) to ensure seamless carrier DLT verification.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Service Implicit, Service Explicit, and Promotional routes?
faqs.a: Service Implicit is for transactional OTPs and alerts delivered 24/7 with zero promotional restriction. Service Explicit is for marketing with customer opt-in. Promotional routes are for bulk marketing sent only between 10:00 AM and 9:00 PM local time.

faqs.q: Why are my India SMS rejected even though the header is registered?
faqs.a: The most common causes are a template mismatch (the message text differs from the approved template, even by punctuation or spacing), a missing or wrong template ID, a URL or call-back number that isn't whitelisted, or a broken PE–TM chain declaration. Check the DLR error code first — it usually points to the failed scrubbing step.

faqs.q: Can a foreign company send SMS to Indian numbers?
faqs.a: Yes. Messages from businesses outside India are carried on international routes, which are priced higher than domestic DLT traffic. If you have an Indian entity, registering on DLT and sending domestically is usually cheaper and more reliable for OTPs.

guideIntro: India runs the world's most structured commercial SMS framework. Under TRAI's Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations (TCCCPR 2018), every business sender must register on a Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) platform operated by the telecom operators — Jio, Airtel, Vi and BSNL. The DLT system checks every message against registered entities, headers and content templates, a process called scrubbing. Messages that don't match are rejected.

Three registrations are needed: the Principal Entity (your business), the header (sender ID) and the content template (approved message text with {#var#} placeholders for variable parts like OTPs). TRAI has added further controls: since late 2024 URLs, APK links and call-back numbers must be whitelisted in templates, and the chain of telemarketers between the business and the operator must be declared (PE–TM chain binding). International traffic to India is handled on separate international routes at different rates.
checklist: Register your Principal Entity on one operator DLT portal (registration is shared across operators).
Register headers: 6-character alphabetic headers for transactional and service messages; numeric headers for promotional messages.
Register content templates with {#var#} placeholders, and whitelist any URL or call-back number used in them.
Declare your telemarketer chain (PE–TM binding) so your traffic is not rejected during scrubbing.
Send the PE ID and template ID with every message (via SMPP TLVs or API parameters).
Send promotional messages only within the permitted daytime window and only to numbers not on the DND registry.

faqs.q: What is the 'RM0.00' prefix requirement in Malaysia?
faqs.a: MCMC regulations mandate that unsolicited promotional text messages include the prefix 'RM0.00' in the message text so recipients know they are not being charged for receiving the SMS.

faqs.q: Can I include links in SMS sent to Malaysia?
faqs.a: Links are heavily filtered in Malaysia because of SMS phishing. Messages with URLs from unverified senders are often blocked. If you need links, use a verified sender and a recognisable domain, and test delivery before a full campaign.

faqs.q: Which networks does a Malaysia SMS route need to reach?
faqs.a: CelcomDigi, Maxis and U Mobile carry most subscribers, with Unifi Mobile and Yes making up the rest. MVNOs run on these networks, so HLR/MNP lookup is used to send each message to the correct operator.

guideIntro: Malaysia's SMS market is regulated by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC). The main operators are CelcomDigi (formed by the 2022 merger of Celcom and Digi), Maxis, U Mobile, and the newer Unifi Mobile and Yes networks, so a route needs coverage on all of them for full reach.

The best-known local rule is the 'RM0.00' prefix: commercial broadcast messages start with RM0.00 to show the recipient is not being charged. Because SMS phishing has been a major issue, Malaysian banks have stopped sending links by SMS, and operators apply strict filtering to messages containing URLs or phone numbers from unverified senders. Personal data in marketing lists is also covered by the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (PDPA).
checklist: Start commercial broadcast messages with the 'RM0.00' prefix.
Register your sender header where required and keep it consistent across campaigns.
Avoid URLs and phone numbers in message bodies unless your sender is verified for them.
Collect consent for marketing under the PDPA and honour opt-out requests.
Send OTPs on transactional routes, never on promotional routes, to avoid filtering delays.
